mechanics.name: Change of Plan
mechanics.currentEffect: Start with 2 Tokens. While inside a Locker and holding a non-event Toolbox, use the Active Ability button to spend 1 Token and transform the Toolbox into a Med-Kit of the same rarity with a random Add-on of the same rarity. The new Med-Kit has 80/90/100% of its charges.
activation: Have a Token and a non-event Toolbox.
Be in a Locker and use the Active Ability button.
Ends/deactivates when: Transformation ends after use; cannot be used without a Token or Toolbox.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (9.4.0): Introduced; no later material live balance change located in the official notes checked.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Spend tokens in a Locker to turn a Toolbox into a same-rarity Med-Kit with a random Add-on.
mechanics.tokenOrStackBehavior: Starts with 2 Tokens; spend 1 per transformation.
specialInteractions: The old Toolbox is replaced by a same-rarity Med-Kit with one random Add-on of that rarity.

editorial.summary: Start with two Tokens and transform a non-event Toolbox in a Locker into a same-rarity Med-Kit with full Tier III charges and a random same-rarity Add-on.
useCases: Use a Toolbox for early objective pressure, then convert it into healing utility later.
Transform a depleted or less-needed Toolbox rather than carrying an irrelevant Item through the rest of the Trial.
Use a second found Toolbox for the remaining Token if the match provides one.
counters: Requires holding a qualifying Toolbox and entering a Locker.
The conversion destroys the Toolbox identity and its Add-ons.
The random Med-Kit Add-on may not suit the situation.
pros: Two Tokens allow another conversion if you acquire another Toolbox.
Same-rarity Med-Kit keeps high-quality Item value.
cons: Requires a Toolbox in the first place.
Locker and conversion setup costs time.
analysis: Change of Plan ranks around the C transition because its best use is clever resource sequencing rather than raw power. A Survivor can bring a Toolbox, spend its useful generator charges early, then convert that Item slot into a Med-Kit later instead of carrying an exhausted resource.

The same-rarity conversion is important. A valuable Toolbox becomes a correspondingly valuable Med-Kit rather than a generic low-grade item, and the Tier III version supplies the new Med-Kit at full charges.
The cost is commitment. The Toolbox is gone, its original Add-ons no longer matter, and the new Add-on is random. You also need a Locker and the correct moment to perform the conversion.

In a deliberate item-economy build, Change of Plan is a neat way to extract two roles from one starting Item. In a normal build, carrying the resource you actually want from the beginning is usually simpler.
editorial.verdict: A flexible item-economy perk for players who want early Toolbox pressure and later healing. Clever, useful, and more complicated than simply bringing the right Item.
